title: End-to-end walkthrough: which process creates which product
blurb: Follow one project from mandate to closure and name the process and activity that creates, updates or approves each management product.
question: A project manager is about to write the plan for the third stage of a four-stage project. In which process and activity is that plan created, and who approves it?

teach.body: Every management product has a home: a process and an activity where it is first created, and points where it is updated or approved. The project manager creates most products in the managing-level processes; team managers create their own in managing product delivery; the project board approves in directing a project. Learn the journey once and most 'which process?' questions answer themselves.

teach.h: The journey of a four-stage project

items.label: Business layer issues the project mandate
Starting up a project, then the board authorizes initiation
Initiating a project, stage boundary, board authorizes the project and stage 2
Controlling a stage + managing product delivery, then a stage boundary each
Controlling a stage + managing product delivery + closing a project
Board authorizes closure; business layer is notified

teach.h: The PM requests, the board authorizes

rows.label: Each boundary
values: Authorize a stage or exception plan

teach.body: Larkspur Building Society's board of directors (the business layer) sends a mandate to refurbish 30 branches. Project manager Nadia Rahman writes the project brief and initiation stage plan in starting up, assembles the PID in initiation and, at each boundary, prepares the next stage plan and end stage report. Her team managers send checkpoint reports; she sends highlight reports. In the final stage she writes the end project and lessons reports, and executive Callum Reid's board authorizes closure.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Project brief = starting up; PID = initiating. (2) The initiation stage plan is made in starting up; every later stage plan in managing a stage boundary. (3) The project plan is created in initiating a project, not in starting up. (4) Exception REPORT comes from controlling a stage; exception PLAN from managing a stage boundary. (5) The lessons log starts in starting up a project, not at closure.

items: Starting up: lessons and daily logs, outline business case, PPD, project approach, team structure, brief, initiation stage plan.
Initiating: management approaches, controls, project plan, full business case, PID.
Delivery: WPDs and highlight and exception reports in CS; team plans and checkpoint reports in MP.
Boundaries: next stage or exception plan, updated plans and business case, end stage report.
Closure: end project report and lessons report; the board authorizes closure in DP.

summary: You can now follow a project from mandate to closure and name where each management product is created, updated and approved. You can also pair each PM request with the board's matching authorization.

A.q: Which process creates the project brief?
A.why: The project brief is assembled in starting up a project (assemble the project brief) and approved by the board in authorize initiation.

whyNot.0: Initiating a project assembles the PID, which supersedes the brief.
whyNot.2: Directing a project approves the brief; it does not create it.
whyNot.3: Managing a stage boundary prepares stage and exception plans.

A.q: Which process creates the project plan?
A.why: The project plan is created in initiating a project (prepare the project plan) and later updated in managing a stage boundary and closing a project.

whyNot.0: Starting up a project creates the initiation stage plan, not the project plan.
whyNot.1: Managing a stage boundary updates the project plan; it does not create it.
whyNot.2: Directing a project approves the project plan as part of the PID.

A.q: Which activity creates the work package description?
options: Authorize a work package, in controlling a stage
Accept a work package, in managing product delivery
Prepare next stage plan, in managing a stage boundary
Establish project controls, in initiating a project
A.why: The PM creates the work package description in authorize a work package, co-creating it with the team manager; the TM then accepts it in managing product delivery.

whyNot.1: Accept a work package is where the TM agrees to it, after the PM has defined it.
whyNot.2: Prepare next stage plan produces the stage plan, not individual work packages.
whyNot.3: Establish project controls sets up control mechanisms for the project, not work packages.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The initiation stage plan is created in starting up a project.
2. The lessons log is first created in closing a project.
3. The full business case is prepared in initiating a project.
4. The exception report is prepared in managing a stage boundary.
B.why: The initiation stage plan comes from starting up a project (1) and the full business case from initiating a project (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the lessons log is created in starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Both are false: the lessons log starts in starting up, and the exception report comes from controlling a stage.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the exception report comes from controlling a stage; the exception plan from managing a stage boundary.

B.q: A project has three stages: initiation and two delivery stages. How many stage plans are produced in managing a stage boundary at planned stage ends?
B.why: The initiation stage plan comes from starting up. The plans for delivery stages 2 and 3 are each produced in managing a stage boundary, so two.

whyNot.0: One misses a delivery stage: each delivery stage needs its own plan from a boundary.
whyNot.2: Three wrongly counts the initiation stage plan, which is made in starting up a project.
whyNot.3: Four is more than the number of stages.

B.q: In which process does the project board approve the project initiation documentation?
B.why: The board approves the PID in directing a project, in the authorize the project activity.

whyNot.0: Initiating a project assembles the PID; the board approves it in directing a project.
whyNot.1: Managing a stage boundary reviews and may update the PID, but approval of the PID is a directing decision.
whyNot.3: Starting up a project produces the brief, before any PID exists.

C.q: Which process and activity create the end stage report?
options: Managing a stage boundary: evaluate the stage
Closing a project: evaluate the project
Managing a stage boundary: request next stage
C.why: The end stage report is produced in managing a stage boundary, in evaluate the stage.

whyNot.1: Report highlights produces highlight reports during the stage.
whyNot.2: Evaluate the project produces the end project report and lessons report.
whyNot.3: Request next stage briefs the board; the report already exists by then.

C.q: Which process creates the exception report, and which creates the exception plan?
options: Managing a stage boundary creates both
Directing a project; managing a stage boundary
Managing a stage boundary; controlling a stage
Controlling a stage; managing a stage boundary
C.why: The PM raises the exception report in controlling a stage (escalate issues and risks) and prepares the exception plan in managing a stage boundary.

whyNot.0: The exception report comes from controlling a stage, not the stage boundary process.
whyNot.1: The board receives exception reports in directing a project; it does not create them.

C.q: Which process creates the lessons log, and which produces the lessons report at the end of the project?
options: Initiating a project; closing a project
Starting up a project; directing a project
Starting up a project; closing a project
Controlling a stage; closing a project
C.why: The lessons log is created in starting up a project (assess previous lessons); the lessons report is produced in closing a project (evaluate the project).

whyNot.0: The lessons log already exists before initiation; it is created in starting up.
whyNot.1: Directing a project is the board's process; the PM produces the lessons report in closing a project.
whyNot.3: The lessons log is created before any delivery stage, in starting up a project.

reteach.title: Following a parcel through the post
reteach.question: If you track a parcel, how do you know where each label and scan comes from?

blocks.body: The sender fills in the label at the counter, the depot adds a sorting record, the van driver scans it out and the recipient signs for it. Each document belongs to one station. PRINCE2 is the same: the brief belongs to starting up, the PID to initiating, work packages to controlling a stage, checkpoint reports to managing product delivery, end stage reports to stage boundaries, and end project reports to closing.

blocks.text: Don't mix up the two 'outline then full' pairs: brief then PID, and outline business case then full business case. The first of each is starting up; the second is initiating.

explain.body: Starting up creates the logs, outline business case, project product description, project approach, team structure, brief and initiation stage plan.

test.q: Which product is created in starting up a project?
test.why: The outline business case is prepared in starting up a project (prepare the outline business case).

whyNot.1: The full business case is prepared in initiating a project.
whyNot.2: The project plan is prepared in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: The PID is assembled in initiating a project.

explain.body: Initiating agrees tailoring and the management approaches, sets controls, prepares the project plan and full business case, and assembles the PID, which is baselined for authorization.

test.q: Which product is assembled in initiating a project and baselined when it is used to gain authorization?
test.why: The PID is assembled in initiating a project; the version used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control (manual 15.4.6).

whyNot.0: The brief is created earlier, in starting up a project.
whyNot.1: The end stage report is produced in managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.2: The mandate comes from the business layer before the project starts.

explain.body: Team managers send checkpoint reports to the PM from managing product delivery. The PM sends highlight reports to the board from controlling a stage.

test.q: Which product does the PM create in controlling a stage to tell the board about stage status?
test.why: The PM produces highlight reports for the board in controlling a stage (report highlights).

whyNot.0: Checkpoint reports come from team managers to the PM.
whyNot.1: The end stage report is produced at a stage boundary.
whyNot.3: An exception plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary at the board's request.

explain.body: In closing a project, evaluate the project produces the end project report, which reviews performance against the PID used to authorize the project, and the lessons report.

test.q: Which product reviews how the project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it?
test.why: The end project report, produced in evaluate the project, reviews performance against the PID version used to authorize the project.

whyNot.0: The lessons report passes on lessons rather than reviewing performance against the PID.
whyNot.1: The end stage report covers a single stage at a boundary.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports give regular stage status during delivery.
